raw_response:
This figure presents two stacked bar charts, labeled (a) and (b), comparing the distribution of Chinese verb senses across four first-level semantic domains—“新闻” (News), “传统文学” (Traditional Literature), “网络小说” (Online Novels), and “微博” (Weibo)—in two distinct linguistic contexts: (a) the distribution of verb senses in various corpora and (b) the distribution of verb senses that are the recipients of passive constructions in various corpora. In both charts, the horizontal axis lists the four semantic domains in the same left-to-right order, while the vertical axis, labeled “频次” (Frequency), is linear and ranges from 0 to 7000, with major tick marks at intervals of 1000. Each bar is segmented into colored portions, with each color corresponding to a specific verb sense category as defined in the legend on the right side of each chart; the legend lists 20 categories with their respective codes and frequencies. In chart (a), the total frequency for each domain is shown at the top of each bar: 4487 for News, 301 for Traditional Literature, 1003 for Online Novels, and 1302 for Weibo. The News bar is dominated by a blue segment (38%, 1700) and a light blue segment (31%, 1400), while the Weibo bar is dominated by a dark blue segment (50%, 650). In chart (b), the total frequencies are 700 for News, 695 for Traditional Literature, 666 for Online Novels, and 6128 for Weibo. The Weibo bar in chart (b) is overwhelmingly dominated by a dark blue segment (80%, 4928), while the other domains show more balanced distributions across multiple segments. The bars in both charts are arranged in the same categorical order and are not sorted by magnitude; no bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or annotations beyond the numerical labels and color coding.
